title: Introduction to Electrical and Electronic Engineering

items.q: A voltage of 6 V is applied across a resistance of 10 ohms. What current flows?
items.s: I = V/R = 6/10 = 0.6 amperes.

items.q: Three resistors of 47, 30 and 20 ohms are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
items.s: In series the resistances add: 47 + 30 + 20 = 97 ohms.

items.q: An appliance draws 0.5 A at 240 V. What is its power consumption in watts?
items.s: P = V I = 240 x 0.5 = 120 watts.

items.q: A steady current of 2 A flows for 10 seconds. What charge has passed, in coulombs?
items.s: Q = I t = 2 x 10 = 20 coulombs.

items.q: Two resistors of 6 ohms and 10 ohms are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?
items.s: Equivalent resistance = R1R2/(R1+R2) = (6 x 10)/(6 + 10) = 3.75 ohms.

items.q: An appliance rated 2 kW runs for 8 hours. If electricity costs N120 per kWh, what is the cost of energy used?
items.s: Energy = 2 kW x 8 h = 16 kWh, so cost = 16 x N120 = N1,920.00.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Control engineering.
o: the branch concerned with systems that regulate themselves to hold a desired output
a material that allows current to flow readily, such as copper
the law that voltage equals current multiplied by resistance
the rate of flow of electric charge, measured in amperes
items.s: Control engineering: the branch concerned with systems that regulate themselves to hold a desired output. The other options describe Electric current, Conductor, Ohm's law.

items.q: Charge is best described as
o: the connection of exposed metalwork to the ground so that fault current flows away safely
the law that a changing magnetic flux induces an electromotive force
the branch concerned with measuring and indicating the variables of a process
the quantity of electricity, measured in coulombs
items.s: Charge: the quantity of electricity, measured in coulombs. The other options describe Earthing, Faraday's law, Instrumentation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Electric shock?
o: an unintended low resistance path that bypasses part of a circuit
the law that voltage equals current multiplied by resistance
a magnet produced by passing current through a coil
the passage of current through the body, which can disturb the heart rhythm
items.s: Electric shock: the passage of current through the body, which can disturb the heart rhythm. The other options describe Electromagnet, Short circuit, Ohm's law.

items.q: The statement “the single resistance that would replace a network with the same effect” describes which of the following?
o: Turns ratio
Equivalent resistance
Fuse
Electromagnet
items.s: Equivalent resistance is the single resistance that would replace a network with the same effect.

items.q: All of the following belong to Network theorems EXCEPT
o: Superposition theorem
Energy
Thevenin's theorem
Norton's theorem
items.s: Every other option belongs to Network theorems. “Energy” belongs to Basic electrical quantities, not Network theorems.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Telecommunication?
o: the branch concerned with transmitting information by electrical or electromagnetic means
the law that voltage equals current multiplied by resistance
current that reverses direction periodically, supplied in Nigeria at fifty hertz
the explosive release of energy when an electric arc forms across a gap
items.s: Telecommunication: the branch concerned with transmitting information by electrical or electromagnetic means. The other options describe Arc flash, Ohm's law, Alternating current.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Rectifier.
o: the single resistance that would replace a network with the same effect
the voltage difference between the feet of a person standing near an earth fault
a circuit that converts alternating current into direct current
the rate of flow of electric charge, measured in amperes
items.s: Rectifier: a circuit that converts alternating current into direct current. The other options describe Step potential, Electric current, Equivalent resistance.

items.q: Transistor is best described as
o: the electrical potential difference that drives current, measured in volts
the explosive release of energy when an electric arc forms across a gap
a switch that opens automatically to protect a circuit from overcurrent
a three-terminal semiconductor device used to amplify or switch signals
items.s: Transistor: a three-terminal semiconductor device used to amplify or switch signals. The other options describe Arc flash, Voltage, Circuit breaker.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Frequency?
o: the law that voltage equals current multiplied by resistance
the number of cycles of an alternating waveform completed in one second
a device that changes alternating voltage by mutual induction between two windings
the branch concerned with systems that regulate themselves to hold a desired output
items.s: Frequency: the number of cycles of an alternating waveform completed in one second. The other options describe Control engineering, Transformer, Ohm's law.

items.q: The statement “the voltage difference between the feet of a person standing near an earth fault” describes which of the following?
o: Step potential
Conductor
Power
Electrical engineering
items.s: Step potential is the voltage difference between the feet of a person standing near an earth fault.

items.q: All of the following belong to Basic electrical quantities EXCEPT
o: Electric current
Voltage
Resistance
Transformer
items.s: Every other option belongs to Basic electrical quantities. “Transformer” belongs to Electromagnetism, not Basic electrical quantities.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Lockout and tagout?
o: the practice of isolating and marking a supply before work so it cannot be re-energised
a material that allows current to flow readily, such as copper
the quantity of electricity, measured in coulombs
a circuit in which the components are connected across the same two points
items.s: Lockout and tagout: the practice of isolating and marking a supply before work so it cannot be re-energised. The other options describe Conductor, Parallel circuit, Charge.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Series circuit.
o: a circuit in which the same current passes through every component one after another
a circuit that converts alternating current into direct current
the principle that the response of a linear circuit to several sources is the sum of the responses to each alone
current that flows in one direction only
items.s: Series circuit: a circuit in which the same current passes through every component one after another. The other options describe Rectifier, Direct current, Superposition theorem.

items.q: Kirchhoff's current law is best described as
o: the number of cycles of an alternating waveform completed in one second
the law that the total current entering a junction equals the total current leaving it
the theorem that any linear network can be replaced by a current source in parallel with a resistance
the theorem that any linear network can be replaced by a single voltage source in series with a resistance
items.s: Kirchhoff's current law: the law that the total current entering a junction equals the total current leaving it. The other options describe Thevenin's theorem, Frequency, Norton's theorem.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Reluctance?
o: the theorem that any linear network can be replaced by a single voltage source in series with a resistance
the quantity of electricity, measured in coulombs
the opposition of a magnetic circuit to the passage of magnetic flux
a circuit in which the components are connected across the same two points
items.s: Reluctance: the opposition of a magnetic circuit to the passage of magnetic flux. The other options describe Parallel circuit, Charge, Thevenin's theorem.

items.q: The statement “a device with a wire that melts to break the circuit when current is excessive” describes which of the following?
o: Electric current
Short circuit
Induced emf
Fuse
items.s: Fuse is a device with a wire that melts to break the circuit when current is excessive.

items.q: All of the following belong to Circuit elements and laws EXCEPT
o: Resistor
Capacitor
Inductor
Short circuit
items.s: Every other option belongs to Circuit elements and laws. “Short circuit” belongs to Direct current circuits, not Circuit elements and laws.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Instrumentation?

a component that stores energy in an electric field, measured in farads
the branch concerned with measuring and indicating the variables of a process
a component that opposes current and drops voltage across it
items.s: Instrumentation: the branch concerned with measuring and indicating the variables of a process. The other options describe Capacitor, Resistor, Arc flash.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Direct current.
o: the result that a load receives maximum power when its resistance equals the source resistance
the branch concerned with transmitting information by electrical or electromagnetic means
a device that trips when it detects current flowing to earth through a fault
current that flows in one direction only
items.s: Direct current: current that flows in one direction only. The other options describe Maximum power transfer, Telecommunication, Residual current device.

items.q: Magnetic field is best described as

the branch concerned with transmitting information by electrical or electromagnetic means
the theorem that any linear network can be replaced by a single voltage source in series with a resistance
a material that allows current to flow readily, such as copper
items.s: Magnetic field: the region around a magnet or current in which magnetic force acts. The other options describe Conductor, Telecommunication, Thevenin's theorem.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Induced emf?
o: the single resistance that would replace a network with the same effect
the theorem that any linear network can be replaced by a single voltage source in series with a resistance
the voltage produced in a conductor by a changing magnetic field
power multiplied by time, sold domestically in kilowatt hours
items.s: Induced emf: the voltage produced in a conductor by a changing magnetic field. The other options describe Thevenin's theorem, Equivalent resistance, Energy.

items.q: The statement “a material whose conductivity lies between that of a conductor and an insulator, such as silicon” describes which of the following?
o: Semiconductor
Electromagnet
Series circuit
Arc flash

Magnetic field
Electric shock
Lenz's law

a material whose conductivity lies between that of a conductor and an insulator, such as silicon
the theorem that any linear network can be replaced by a single voltage source in series with a resistance
the law that the sum of voltage drops around a closed loop equals zero

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Transformer.
o: the branch concerned with the control of electric current in devices such as diodes and transistors
the result that a load receives maximum power when its resistance equals the source resistance
the branch concerned with the generation, transmission and distribution of bulk electrical energy
a device that changes alternating voltage by mutual induction between two windings
items.s: Transformer: a device that changes alternating voltage by mutual induction between two windings. The other options describe Maximum power transfer, Electronics, Power engineering.

items.q: Open circuit is best described as
o: a break in the path so that no current can flow
current that flows in one direction only
the result that a load receives maximum power when its resistance equals the source resistance
the rate at which electrical energy is used or delivered, measured in watts
items.s: Open circuit: a break in the path so that no current can flow. The other options describe Power, Maximum power transfer, Direct current.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Voltage?
o: the law that the sum of voltage drops around a closed loop equals zero
a circuit in which the components are connected across the same two points
the principle that the response of a linear circuit to several sources is the sum of the responses to each alone
the electrical potential difference that drives current, measured in volts

Faraday's law
Norton's theorem
Control engineering

current that flows in one direction only
the branch concerned with the control of electric current in devices such as diodes and transistors

items.q: Which of the following best describes Inductor?
o: the opposition a material offers to the flow of current, measured in ohms
the electrical potential difference that drives current, measured in volts
a component that stores energy in a magnetic field, measured in henries
a circuit in which the same current passes through every component one after another
items.s: Inductor: a component that stores energy in a magnetic field, measured in henries. The other options describe Voltage, Resistance, Series circuit.

Insulator

Transformer

o: the practice of isolating and marking a supply before work so it cannot be re-energised
the passage of current through the body, which can disturb the heart rhythm
the voltage difference between the feet of a person standing near an earth fault
a device that trips when it detects current flowing to earth through a fault
items.s: Residual current device: a device that trips when it detects current flowing to earth through a fault. The other options describe Step potential, Electric shock, Lockout and tagout.
